title: salix exigua subsp. interior
intro: Salix exigua subsp. interior, commonly known as the Coyote Willow, is a subspecies of deciduous shrub or small tree native to the southwestern United States and northwestern Mexico. This plant is used in traditional medicine to treat various health conditions, with reported health benefits including relief from fever, cough, and respiratory issues. The therapeutic actions of Salix exigua subsp. interior include anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and expectorant properties, which help to reduce inflammation, combat infections, and relieve congestion. The bioactive constituents of this plant include salicin, a compound similar to aspirin, as well as other flavonoids, terpenoids, and phenolic acids that contribute to its medicinal properties.
